reviews.text: Sadly, we had to have our very elderly budgie, Guus, put to sleep last week. We were deeply impressed by the loving and empathetic way the veterinarian acted, making it a very special moment for us. Moreover, a few days ago, a handwritten card wishing us well arrived in the mail. Thank you so much for the years of excellent care!

I have been bringing my dog to Dierenkliniek IJburg for the past 3 years, and I have always been happy with the veterinary care itself. Unfortunately, my experience with the front desk, particularly with the same receptionist, has been extremely disappointing.

This is also not the first time I have experienced this kind of behavior from her. There have been several occasions where I have had similar problems with the same person — unnecessary attitude, poor communication, and making simple requests much more difficult than they need to be. I have tried to be patient and understanding, but today was really the point where I felt I had to speak up.

This morning, after my dog’s appointment, I asked the receptionist for an invoice. She told me she would send it to me. When I still hadn’t received it in the afternoon, I called. During my first call, she hung up on me. I called again, and she apologized and said she had tried to send it but that it wasn’t working, and promised to send it immediately.

Several hours later, I still had not received anything. I called again, and as soon as she recognized my voice, she put me on hold for around 20 minutes. At that point, I decided to go to the clinic personally.

When I arrived, instead of simply helping me, she was extremely rude and started giving me explanations about how busy they were and that a colleague was sick. I completely understand that a clinic can be busy and that a colleague may be absent, but that does not justify treating a customer disrespectfully.

I simply asked her to print the invoice for me. She eventually printed it, and I said, “It wasn’t that difficult.” After that, she became extremely angry, raised her voice, and started shouting at me, saying that she did not like my attitude.

The whole interaction was completely unacceptable and very upsetting. I was still hearing her shouting after I had left and closed the door.

I am particularly disappointed because I have been a client for 3 years and have never had an issue with the veterinary care. My issue is specifically with the way I have repeatedly been treated by this receptionist.

I hope the owner/management reads this review and takes it seriously, because this is clearly not an isolated incident. I have experienced similar situations with the same person several times, and today it went too far.

Customers deserve to be treated with basic respect and professionalism. Being busy is understandable, but being rude, hanging up on customers, putting them on hold without explanation, and shouting at them is not acceptable customer service.

We have been taking our red-tailed parrot to this clinic for years. They are well-specialized in birds. But over the years, you could see things change. Poor communication, and making an appointment for the bird is difficult.

Our red-tailed parrot was at the clinic last week for his annual check-up. Everything was fine, but he is biting his legs bare. He received a vitamin injection and medication for one week.
If it didn't work, we were to make a new appointment after one week.
But this is a problem; there is no availability. We have to call every day to see if we can get in.
We work and cannot do this, but the most important thing is that the little animal is very itchy and there is no space.
Furthermore, they are not making any effort to find a solution.
We are now going to another clinic, but I feel that this has been handled very poorly.
It is such a shame; we were always satisfied, and so was our bird.
We have a cockatoo and go here because, in our opinion, it is the most suitable vet for her. Friendly to both the owner and the animals.

I visited the clinic because I thought my beloved cat might have a urinary blockage. First, I called them because I needed emergency care, but they told me that their emergency service was completely full. I found that very strange. They simply told me to look for another emergency clinic on my own. I called a different emergency clinic, and they helped me.
However, I still wanted to make sure my cat was okay, so I booked an appointment and went to this clinic. By that time, a urine sample had already been collected for analysis. The results showed that there were no urinary crystals, and his urine pH was 7, which is normal for a stressed and frightened cat. My cat hates leaving the house, and he becomes extremely anxious outside. He was so scared that he even urinated on the way to the clinic.
After I left, the clinic called me and said they wanted to perform a blood test to check his kidneys, even though the urine test results were already sufficient. I asked them whether it was absolutely necessary because my cat is extremely fearful, and I did not want to put him through that stress again. They replied that it might be needed because of a future dental cleaning. I honestly don’t understand what that has to do with the current issue. It just seemed like another expensive, unnecessary test. The urine crystal analysis alone cost €142.
When I returned home, I noticed that my cat had started scratching himself excessively and was losing fur around his face, which strongly suggests that he developed an infection. My cat never goes outside and has no contact with other cats, so there is no logical way he could have caught an infection except at the clinic. When I placed him on the examination table, I noticed hair from another animal still on it. It seemed that the table had not been properly cleaned or disinfected before my cat was examined, and I firmly believe that this is how he became infected.
Afterward, I contacted the clinic through WhatsApp and asked if they could help me, since my language skills are not good enough to explain everything over the phone. They never replied. It honestly feels as though they see these innocent animals only as a source of money and do not truly care about their pain or well-being.
I am heartbroken for my cat. It deeply saddens me to see innocent animals suffer because of negligence, lack of compassion, and a system that seems to view beloved pets as nothing more than a way to make money.Based on my experience, I would not recommend this clinic. I hope they improve their standards of care, communication, and hygiene so that other animals do not have to go through what my cat experienced.

Terrible practice, they take no responsibility. Went with a macaw for a blood test. Called after 3 weeks, told: "You will be called this afternoon by the vet with the results."
Heard nothing, and the next day received the message: Blood lost. They take no responsibility and blame the courier. No apologies and no understanding for the macaw. The answer was: just have it drawn again. They don't care that the macaw finds this very unpleasant. The only thing they say is: we can't do anything about it. It is not our fault.

No empathy.
Had it drawn again the next day anyway; no empathy towards the bird, absolutely no communication except: "I'll just take him with me for a moment and here he is back."
To make matters worse, called that same afternoon with the news that the previous blood test had been found after all.
How is that even possible!!! So incompetent, never again Dierenkliniek IJburg.

After having to call because I didn’t receive a confirmation email, the person on the phone confirmed that my appointment was at 15:30. I received then the confirmation email that I didn’t read because I just had the person on the phone. When I got there they told me that my appointment was at 16’30 so I had to wait an hour there, because reschedule would cost me 49e fee.

Highly recommend this vet clinic to anyone living in IJburg or nearby. The team is very professional and caring, easily can switch to English if it is still hard to negotiate in Dutch. I saw how my pets felt at ease even during vaccinations or blood collection, which I believe is a solid green flag. Be sure that you'll receive the best services here.

I took my grey parrot to be examined and have his wings clipped, but it seems the doctor who examined him understands nothing about birds. She clipped more than half of his wings in a brutal and incorrect way, and the bird watches as it is clipped and the feathers fall out. This has put the bird in a psychological state from which I can no longer rescue him. He no longer likes to be close to people; she is a stupid doctor! She gave me instructions on feeding and caring for parrots, and after I investigated and verified them, I discovered that most of the information she spoke about was incorrect and unfounded. I do not recommend taking your birds there.
They mucked up the appointment time and told us to come back 4 hrs later, but they managed to squeeze us in , do in the end they were good
This is a top-notch vet. Pieth Olaf felt thoroughly pampered by you. Thank you for that, and see you again for sure.

I don't like posting negative reviews, but in this case, I feel it is important.

I have a noble parrot that I have felt for years was declining. At Ijburglaan, she was put through the mill and declared healthy.

Nevertheless, it didn't feel right, and I kept coming back. The 'symptoms' worsened, and I was told that these were likely behavioral problems.

Until about a year ago, when she stopped eating.

She had an infection, metal poisoning, psittacosis, and PDD. Of which, I was now told, the metal poisoning was already visible in the X-rays 3 years ago (but which I had not been told).

Surgery was considered, but by then I had lost my trust, so I switched to the University of Utrecht Veterinary Clinic.

The diagnosis there was gastritis. Because the treatment was not working, we had a gastroscopy performed.

What did it reveal? Luna (my parrot), that poor little creature, has seen one of the worst stomach infections ever. This has been going on for years.

Now we are in a difficult process that will last for years. What I spent at Ijburg over the past few years hoping for answers, I have now had to spend at Utrecht within half a year to do whatever it takes because I want to get Luna through this. The metal poisoning also turns out to be complete nonsense and has now been ruled out with certainty.

I cannot speak ill of the people who work there because I want to believe that everyone there has their heart in the right place. Nevertheless, I get furious when I think of this practice because they could have prevented us from suffering so much.

So;
If you have doubts about your animal's symptoms, go to Utrecht or elsewhere, because at Ijburg they stick to their answers, even if it comes at the expense of your animal.

The vet prescribed daily Metacam/Meloxicam (associated with acute renal failure in cats that have kidney disease and experience dehydration - dehydration is not purely not drinking - it is also when the kidneys cannot concentrate urine properly) to my elderly cat with arthritis that presented with several symptoms of kidney disease. I was never given an option to give informed consent - as alternative treatments were never fully presented to me, neither were the risks of Metacam mentioned. The vet only did bloodwork - which was "perfect" - however kidney disease often doesn't show up in blood tests until 75% of kidney function is lost. A urianalysis is how kidney function can be measured, as well as an ultrasound. None of those were suggested by the vet.

I was also refused a check-in after 2 weeks of starting Metacam (which I asked for after reading studies on the risks of Metacam/Meloxicam) and was told to come back in 6 months.

My cat was diagnosed with arthritis, only based on the blood test and physical exam.

My cat started deteriorating rapidly in around 4-5 weeks after Metacam was prescribed. His Creatinine was 1352 (around 13 times the norm) and I admitted him to an emergency hospital where he spent 2 weeks and was stabilized - however his kidneys were at that point damaged beyond healing, he had cachexia, nausea, anemia, mouth ulcers, nausea. After 1 week at home we had to euthanize him as he kept deteriorating.

The conclusion of the other doctors was that my cat already had underlying issues, most likely kidney issues, before starting on Metacam - considering his creatinine was stabilized from 1352 to 360 with daily IV fluids, and many other treatments, and that it jumped to 550 with weight loss of 600 grams in 6 days in his last week of life.

Those kidney issues could have been diagnosed - but the vet from this clinic was ignorantly confident that there were no kidney problems with my cat. That cost my cat his life. Ignorance when you treat animals or people is not excusable and I hope that this vet will think twice before deciding not to run urine tests on aging cats - kidney disease is one of three leading causes of death in cats - and prescribing an NSAID such as Metacam/Meloxicam. The vets, out of all people, should know that cats rarely even present with symptoms - as they hide their illness well.

I hope the vet will think twice before not allowing the owner to give INFORMED consent because that is exactly what you did, and I hope you will be able to take responsibility for your mistakes and think more critically in the future, because if you don't - your mistakes will lead to more pet deaths.

General advice - do not bring your pet here. They may get treated and be fine but they may also die because of the incompetence and ignorance.
